corePrinciple: The fighting is the hook. Tactical mechanics create depth. Progression creates long-term retention.
primaryExperience: The primary screen and primary player memory must be the deity battle, not menu management.
combatFeelRequirements: Every attack must communicate physical contact through animation, VFX, hit stop, enemy reaction, and damage feedback.
Powerful deity attacks must alter the camera, environment, enemy pose, or battlefield state before the player reads damage numbers.
Ability availability, cooldown, status effects, and target validity must be visible without hiding the battlefield.
Combat decisions must be made from the battlefield view whenever possible. Secondary panels explain; they do not replace fighting.
titanPowerRules: Every deity needs a recognizable combat silhouette and attack identity beyond damage and health.
Each deity kit must express range, mobility, survivability, battlefield interaction, and signature moment potential.
Legendary scale is shown through enemy reactions, environmental response, large readable animations, and distinct impact cadence.
No deity may be differentiated only by stat deltas.
tacticalDepthRules: Add mechanics only when they create an interesting combat decision.
A good turn asks where to move, who to attack, whether to spend or save an ability, whether to defend, and how to manipulate enemy position.
Difficulty should rise through smarter positioning, enemy intent, objective pressure, battlefield layout, timing, and boss mechanics before raw stats.
Avoid one obvious optimal button by mixing target priority, range pressure, terrain opportunity, cooldown timing, and objective risk.
battlefieldRules: Every battlefield section must have a gameplay purpose: open combat area, choke, flank, elevation, landmark, hazard, objective zone, or cover rhythm.
Beautiful environments without tactical function are rejected for core combat arenas.
3D layouts must preserve deity scale with readable lanes, large landmarks, and cinematic camera anchors.
Battlefield interaction must support force movement, area attacks, protection plays, and comeback moments.
uiRules: Battlefield visibility outranks every secondary menu.
Basic combat actions must not require multi-menu navigation.
Primary UI shows deity, health, movement, targets, ability availability, cooldowns, statuses, and objectives.
Secondary statistics must be collapsible or contextual and never dominate the battlefield.
progressionRules: Progression exists to make players excited to return to battle.
Unlocks, shards, gear, upgrades, faction bonuses, bosses, events, and async defense must each answer what new combat expression they create.
Reject spreadsheet-feeling progression that delays fighting without changing combat feel.
Upgrade prompts should make the player want to see what the deity does in battle.
replayabilityRules: Replayability must come from enjoyable fighting first, then difficulty, elite encounters, bosses, events, async defense, divine mastery, team combinations, and battlefield variations.
Repeat modes must vary tactical problems rather than only increasing stats.
Campaign completion should open better fights, not just larger checklists.
playerExperienceQuestions: Is the player spending most of their time doing something fun?
Would the player willingly play another battle immediately?
systemServiceTest: Every system must make the deity battle more fun, more tactical, more satisfying, or more replayable. If it does not, reconsider whether it belongs in the core experience.

acceptanceGates.rule: Playable Ops and future game views must present battle selection/simulation before management statistics.
Deity differentiation must include attack identity, ability behavior, range/mobility/role expression, or battlefield interaction.
Battlefield data and mission profiles must expose tactical purpose, objective pressure, or terrain function.
Progression framing must explicitly return the player to battle instead of menu management.
Difficulty guidance must prefer AI, positioning, objective, layout, timing, boss, and composition levers before stats.
Combat design must target cinematic memorable events during battles.

sourceDirective: Holder combat-first gameplay design directive, August 16 2026
